outcome.description: tests = the tests below are ready for the gates; escalate = robust tests are not possible at this complexity

risk.description: Required when outcome is tests. How much of what the refactoring could break the tests protect

level.description: low = every way the change could break behavior, and every plan point, is covered by a test that survives the refactoring; medium = gaps a reviewer of the diff would likely catch; high = an uncovered breakage would likely reach production

uncovered.description: Each breakage or plan point no test covers, in plain words

reasoning.description: Why the level is what it is: what is protected, what is not, and why the gaps could not be closed without changing production code

proposed_complexity.description: Set when the item is harder to protect than its complexity rating suggests

coverage.description: Required when outcome is tests. How the tests cover what the change could break

breakages.description: Every realistic way a mistake in carrying out the plan would change observable behavior, from each step's 'Can break' notes applied to this code. Behavior the plan does not touch is not listed, however important it is

name.description: The mistake and what it would break, in plain words, e.g. 'IEstimateRepository is not registered, so the handler cannot be created and every estimate email fails'

step.description: The plan step a mistake would come from, e.g. steps[0]

tests.description: Fully qualified names of the declared tests that would fail if it happened

not_covered.description: Why no test that survives the refactoring can catch it; any uncovered breakage means the risk is not low

plan_points.description: One entry for every element of the plan's change_points and risks

name.description: Fully qualified test method name: Namespace.Class.Method

file.description: Test file you wrote, relative to the repository root

kind.description: unit = the class or method under test with fakes for injectable dependencies, no database, container, or mediator; integration = anything larger: the wiring test, or a test flagged needs_refactor

wiring.description: true only for the single wiring test per item: it builds the real container, resolves the changed type through its entry point, and asserts an outcome only the correct implementation, sharing the request's state, produces

needs_refactor.description: Required on every integration test that is not the wiring test. Marks a test that is valid before and after the refactoring but expensive to keep (a database, the container, the mediator, or long setup), written because no cheaper test can reach the behavior today. It is rewritten after the implementation

reason.description: Why a cheaper test is not possible on the current code: the missing seam, e.g. 'repositories are created with new from CRMContext inside the constructor'

after_refactor.description: The cheaper test that should replace it once the refactoring creates the seam, e.g. 'construct with a fake IOpportunityRepository whose GetById throws for deleted records'

behavior.description: The observable behavior the test pins, in plain words (no test or code names)

protects.description: The mistake in carrying out the plan that this test catches, and the step it would come from

why.description: Why breaking this behavior would matter

sabotage.description: A small change to production code that breaks the protected behavior; the test must fail with it applied

find.description: Exact text that occurs once in the file
